correctness.rationale: An exact disjoint-source decomposition gives score \(k+B(L)+B(R)+\sum_i G(g_i)\); independent-edge events in each interior gap yield \(G(g)=2\sum_{j=1}^g p^j-gp^{g+1}\). Direct subtraction proves decreasing marginal lists \(b_t=p^t\) and \(h_t=p^t[1+t(1-p)]\), hence global prefix-merging optimality. The worst occupied interior marginal under optimally balanced endpoint placement is \(h_q\) and the best unoccupied outer marginal is \(p\). This proves the global endpoint iff test and, by F_q derivative, its unique nontrivial crossing and phase claims. A uniform-fixed-c logarithmic expansion yields \(1-p_q\sim2/q^2\). The packaged Python 3 checker independently enumerated source and percolation configurations and ran 6,546 finite assertions/diagnostics. Unproved scope: general graphs, other epidemic observables or empirical performance.

value.rationale: The exact global placement rule, all-\(n\) critical endpoint phase and 2/q^2 boundary scale identify an analytically motivated reversal between terminal and interior monitoring in homogeneous epidemics on linear networks. They are not a textbook restatement of submodularity, a numerical-only witness, or a tiny arbitrary parameter adjustment: the complete structural classification is reusable as a benchmark. Its utility does not imply empirical recommendations for nonpath networks or time-sensitive surveillance.
